title: The library the phone uses to hand a picture or file to other apps is flagged by the dependency scan
what: Sharing a workout picture or a routine file goes through the phone's sharing library. The dependency scan marks the installed version as a moderate risk, through a build-time setup package it pulls in. The scan says the fix is a major upgrade of that library. Nothing has written down whether the flagged part ever runs on a member's phone.
expected: The sharing library has no open alerts, or the alert is checked and written down as build-time only and not reachable on the phone.
who: members who share a workout picture or a routine
how_often: unknown; the flagged part looks build-time only
fix_line: Confirm the flagged part only runs while building the app; move to the newer sharing library with the next Expo upgrade.

items.reason: No file in this area calls the server itself (no database client, RPC or fetch). The one server read it starts is the gym-plans sync on the Workout tab, which calls member_gym_plans: owner-run with a fixed search path, open to anon and signed-in callers by design, and it only answers for the gym tied to the member's own key after the phone, roster and name checks. The tab bar, share picture and up-next pieces only read gym details the shop stores already fetched.

Tables behind member_gym_plans: crm_records and gym_members have row rules on and no policies, so the apps cannot read them at all; gyms has only a same-gym read policy. The only way in is member_gym_plans, and test 8 proves a member of another gym with the same phone number gets nothing of this gym's plans. Everything else in the area (photos, routines, folders, settings) lives in the phone's own database.
Rule applied: the server tables this area reaches through member_gym_plans have a cross-gym test, so no finding.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only the existing database test was read.
The secrets scan has no hits in this area and the area's files hold no keys or web addresses other than the YouTube rule for trainer videos.
No AI or paid-service key is used here; the AI coach entry in settings is only an on/off switch kept on the phone.
No sign-in, PIN or session handling in these workout, profile and settings components.

Text boxes are the rest-time digits (numbers only, 2 long), the set boxes (line breaks stripped) and the folder name, which goes to the phone's own database through placeholder-bound queries; all are shown back as plain text, never as web page code. The trainer's video link is opened only if it passes the YouTube-only rule, checked again at the tap.

Workout photos and exercise photos or videos are picked from the camera or gallery and copied into the app's own storage; nothing is uploaded. Exercise videos are capped at 30 seconds and 80 MB, workout photos at 4.
No link is made here: routines and workouts are shared as text, a file or a picture, with no gym page or join-code link in them. The only link opened is a trainer's YouTube video.

Of the outside libraries this area loads, the scan flags two: the screen-navigation library (high; already a finding) and the sharing library (moderate; new finding). The other libraries used here have no alerts. The repo has no dependency alerts switched on (already a finding).
